prompt_en: Photograph a complex myth-creature tableau in a contemporary museum's black-box kinetic diorama, where composite myth creatures hold a suspended encounter with connected forms visible together. On the left, a human head or upper body belongs to the selected Greek Siren, realized as one explicitly fictional adult woman's head and neck entering a feathered avian trunk. Here a bird body wings and feet form the same creature lower structure: two feathered wings spread from visible roots, two scaly legs with talons gripping a low stone block, and a continuous feathered tail. At the visible neck-to-feather junction, the human and avian parts join coherently in one connected creature. Her dark brown eyes, soft oval face, straight short dark bob and wispy bangs take visible appearance cues from the attached portrait. She faces the camera with her mouth gently parted as if her song has just stopped. The siren is framed with her neck-to-feather seam, both wing roots and taloned feet unobstructed against the dark curtain. On the right, a lion body and forward lion head form one connected Chimera, standing in three-quarter profile on four feline paws with a tawny torso and mane. A horned goat neck rises vertically from the middle lion spine: a separate goat head grows from the middle of that same back. At the visible rump attachment, the tail of that same creature ends in a snake head; its continuous scaly course curves into the open right side of the stage. An empty crescent of stage surrounds the chimera's dorsal goat-neck insertion and rump-to-serpent curve. The two creatures face across a clear strip of floor, each body's contour separated from the other. Warm stage light reveals the siren's face and layered feathers, while cooler illumination reveals the lion fur, goat neck and serpent scales. Photograph both entire creatures in one horizontal frame from modestly elevated chest height, keeping all body junctions, claws, paws and tail tips in focus. Black curtains and a worn stage floor give the pair the tactile presence of museum animatronics.
